message: No detected untrusted source handling: The code reads from local files and a bundled JSON resource (cards.collectible.json) without any checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks on remote sources.

No detected label flipping detection: The code assigns class labels based on deck card data (ingameClass) but performs no comparison of label distributions, validation against an expected label set, or label-noise detection.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The only data integrity check is a card-count validation (len(deck.cardList) != 30), which is a basic structural check rather than outlier detection, statistical anomaly analysis, or poisoning-specific filtering.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads external resources (cards.collectible.json, hearthstone card database via load_dbf) without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision; no serialized model weights are loaded with integrity controls.

No detected label distribution validation: The code parses deck data into class lists and checks for 30-card lists, but there is no validation of label distribution, class balance, or expected label set before training/clustering begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural-cleanse-style trigger detection, activation-pattern analysis, or any other backdoor defense in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries or mechanisms (e.g., Opacus, TF Privacy, DP-SGD) are imported or used anywhere in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: There is no use of adversarial testing frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) or any robustness stress tests anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no isolation of a held-out test set from training data, no hashing or signing of evaluation data, and no use of multiple independent metrics to guard against metric manipulation.

No detected input sanitization: The code reads CSV input and parses deck strings without any schema validation, range checks, or rejection logic beyond a basic card-count check (len==30) and a bare try/except that silently continues on parse errors.

No detected output bounds checks: There are no checks on the classification outputs returned by testClassify(); no probability bounds, NaN guards, or threshold validation are applied before results are used.

No detected prompt injection defenses: This is not an LLM-based pipeline; it performs deck clustering/classification on Hearthstone deck codes, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
